rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: We don't have much time, Pela! Bronya wants to get everyone's opinion.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Wait, you're telling me I have to make this huge decision on the spot? At least give me a few seconds to think it over.
rows.speaker: Pela

rows.text: Okay, I think I've got it.
rows.speaker: Pela

rows.text: If it were up to me... I'd probably agree to the IPC's conditions.
rows.speaker: Pela

rows.text: Huh, okay... Any particular reason?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I've looked at some of the climate reports, and based on the data I've seen, it'll take three or four more generations for the snow to completely subside.
rows.speaker: Pela

rows.text: And that's assuming no other disasters occur. I care more about those in the present than a future I can't be sure of.
rows.speaker: Pela

rows.text: If the IPC is able to bring about immediate change, then I think that's a price well worth paying.
rows.speaker: Pela

rows.text: Building a better world for future generations sound great, right? But is it any fun for the engineers and Architects who are directly involved in such a pursuit?
rows.speaker: Pela

rows.text: I see. So compared to a distant and uncertain future, what you really care about is making sure the people around you have a good life...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Thanks for your input. I'll make a note of your opinion.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Is that [Trailblazer] and Miss March? It's been a while! I didn't think you'd be back in Belobog so soon.
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: It's been pretty hectic in the city lately. All these people dressed in black suddenly showed up, and even the Silvermane Guards have had trouble dealing with them...
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: We need your opinion on an important matter.
You need my opinion? Happy to help.
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: You tell Dunn about the IPC debt and the choice facing Bronya...
...So that's who they are. Huh, it's worse than I imagined.
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: The Madam Guardian must be under a lot of pressure... Is there really nothing we can do to assist her?
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: We're here to gather everyone's opinion on the matter. I know this is a little sudden, but we're running out of time. What's your take?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Why, I'd refuse the contract, of course! There is no room for compromise!
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: Just look at them — arrogant, stomping around here as if they own the place. How can such people be trusted? Who's to say they won't breach the contract?
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: Faced with this sort of coercion, we must resist them with all our might! Surrendering is not an option!
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: You must warn the Madam Guardian not to allow herself to fall into their trap!
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: A soldier's perspective is always valuable, Dunn.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Thanks for your input. I'll make a note of your opinion.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Did we miss anyone in the Overworld? I think we asked just about everyone we needed to.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: From what I've gathered, it seems like most people in the Overworld are leaning towards signing the IPC's contract.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: We'd better hurry to the Underworld and see what Natasha and Seele make of it all...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Miss March, [Trailblazer], what brings you two to the Underworld? And why the long face?
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: We need your opinion on an important matter.
Seems a little out of the blue, but since you came all this way, it must be urgent. Go ahead.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: You tell Natasha about the IPC debt and the choice facing Bronya...
That's a lot of information to take in. Sorry, both of you — I know you're in a hurry, but I need a moment to think.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: No stress, Nat. Just tell us what you really think.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I've thought about it, and... Well, if I were Bronya, I wouldn't sign it.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: I won't deny, the offer on the table is a very tempting one... and if we refuse, Belobog will not only have the burden of a huge debt — we may also incite the wrath of a very powerful force...
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: ...but even so, a quote I read back in school came to me just now: "Those who are willing to give up freedom for security will end up with neither."
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Living in the Underworld has taught me that this phrase is true. I'd rather trek through the frigid Snow Plains than live in a beautiful cage.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: ...Wow, that's a pretty convincing argument...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Another vote for the against pile. Thanks for your insight, Nat.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Miss March, {F#big sister}{M#big brother} [Trailblazer]! What brings you to the Underworld?
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Hey there, Clara! Huh? Is Svarog not around?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Mr. Svarog went out for a walk with a lady called Topaz...
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: What!? Topaz!? Do you know where they went?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I'm not sure... but Mr. Svarog promised he'd be back soon...
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Ugh! What now, [Trailblazer]? Svarog's super logical, we should definitely get his opinion...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: At least Clara's here.
Clara's opinion is just as important!
True. Dan Heng's always saying that Clara's really insightful for her age.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Huh? Miss March, do you want to ask me something?
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: You tell Clara about the IPC debt and the choice facing Bronya...
Uhh... That's complicated... I don't know what to say...
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: It's alright, Clara, no pressure. Just tell us how you feel about it.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I... I think if we have a choice for the future, it should be everyone's decision.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Because... when I was playing with Hook, The Moles, and the other kids... We talked about our dreams...
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Everyone has different dreams. If we accept Miss Topaz's offer, then doesn't that mean our dreams will never come true?
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Just taking away people's dreams like that... I don't know... It feels wrong.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: You're right. Children see the world as a place where anything is possible...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...just the thought of our lives being predestined from birth makes me shiver!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Thanks, Clara. Your thoughts mean a lot to us.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: None other than the saviors of Belobog! To what do I owe the pleasure? To be honest, I'm surprised you even remembered an old geezer like me!
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: But... I can tell by the look on your faces you're probably not dropping by to say hi.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: We need your opinion on an important matter.
Let me guess — something to do with these unruly people in black showing up everywhere?
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Well, ask away! It just so happens I'm curious about them myself. Maybe I can be of some help.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: You tell Oleg about the IPC debt and the choice facing Bronya...
I see...
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: ...That's a tricky situation alright... a lot for anyone to handle, let alone someone as young as Lady Bronya.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Mr. Oleg, out of all the people we know in Belobog, you have the most life experience. What do you think we should do?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Wanna hear the truth? I'm afraid great ambitions and lofty plans no longer hold much appeal for an old-timer like me.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: If this "IPC" does indeed possess the magical power to restore Belobog back to its former self overnight, then I think the answer is clear.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Have you considered the opposite? What about if we refuse? The reconstruction plan already sounds like an endless endeavor. With the added burden of a massive debt... How's that something we can manage on our own?
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: What worries me most is how Lady Bronya will handle the backlash from her people. Will she be able to withstand the criticism? Is she prepared to carry the weight of a tarnished reputation for years to come?
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Bronya... "The Last Supreme Guardian..."
I think she can handle a little criticism.
Huh, I guess I never looked at it from that angle... I wouldn't wish that title on anyone.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I think so too. But could you imagine having to hear names like "The Traitorous Ruler" for the rest of your life?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Thank you for your thoughts, Mr. Oleg. Another vote for the "for" pile.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: After collecting more citizen opinions, the final result remains a tie...
Whew... All that running around has worn me out.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: So, the final conclusion is...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...The votes are completely even! Ugh, I don't know what to do — both sides have really compelling arguments.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: There's still one person left to ask.
Only Bronya can make the final call.
Right! We haven't asked Seele!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Wait a minute, we forgot to ask Seele! Let's go see what she has to say.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: She's probably still in the Great Mine helping the miners. Come on, let's get going!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Back so soon? Any news?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: A—Are you feeling alright, [Trailblazer]? You look a little uneasy.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: We need your opinion on an important matter.
Important matter, huh...?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: I can tell from your tone this isn't gonna be a lighthearted chat... but I'm ready to hear it.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: You tell Seele about the IPC debt and the choice facing Bronya...
I... think I get it. At first, I thought it was just a few IPC ruffians overstepping their boundaries...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Yeah, you didn't think the future of Belobog was at stake, right?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Right... I need a little time to process this...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: As it stands, the votes are even. Your opinion will make all the difference.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...In that case... I... I abstain.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Huh!?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Your vote is extremely important...
You have to shoulder this responsibility.
I've thought about it... This responsibility rests on Bronya's shoulders, not mine.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: No, this responsibility rests on Bronya's shoulders, not mine.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: No matter the choice she makes, she has far greater foresight than I do — she can see the bigger picture more clearly than I can.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: The vote is tied. If I were to give you my view, it would tip the scales and possibly impact her final choice.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: I'll respect whatever decision she makes, but... it's not my place to make it for her.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: ...Understood, Seele. This is a difficult decision to make, and everyone feels differently about it.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It's times like these that a leader must stand up and do what's needed...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Right... It's Bronya's decision. She knows what's at stake — she won't run away from her duty. I trust her wholeheartedly.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: If she asks you, just let her know my reasoning. She'll understand.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Well, it's all in Bronya's hands now. She has to make the final call.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: She plays a crucial role on this world.
Do you trust her judgment?
Right? I'm glad Belobog has someone like her in charge...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You bet! The Express can vouch for Bronya. That says a lot about her character.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The time has come — let's go fill her in. I'm curious to see how she's handling those Qlipoth ministers.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Wait a sec, did Gepard say that he's in Rivet Town? Could that mean Topaz is...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: No time for guesses! Let's just head to Rivet Town and find Gepard first.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Gepard should be waiting for us in Rivet Town, right?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Here we go again, back to our old stomping grounds for another adventure!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Mr Svarog! Are you alright? I hope Topaz and her IPC henchmen didn't hurt you.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Greetings, outsiders. System functions are normal — I have had no conflict with the IPC's representatives.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: I thought we might be facing off against each other for a moment.
Such a result would be highly undesirable.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: Topaz is ahead. She had the means to force me to comply with her orders, but chose not to.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: From her perspective, the only way to "preserve" Belobog is by incorporating it into the IPC. While I do not agree with her viewpoint, I lack the computational power to provide evidence to the contrary.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: While it is unlikely, I still encourage the avoidance of any potential conflicts.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: "Unlikely, potential..." meaning there could still be conflicts...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Don't worry, March. The Express never pursues conflict as a first means... but if it comes down to it, we won't back down either. That's how it's always been.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Himeko's right. As long as we can look at ourselves in the mirror and know we did the right thing, that's all that matters.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Kyle, sorry for the delay. Are we clear to proceed?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: The path ahead is clear, Madam Guardian. You and your companions can proceed north without hindrance.
rows.speaker: Soldier Kyle

rows.text: Excellent. The mountain road ahead is a little treacherous, watch your step.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...Let's go.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Miss Topaz, you mentioned accountability...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Don't worry, it's nothing I can't handle. There are more important things than titles and ranks — finding the best solution is what matters most.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: Will they cut your pay?
Won't you get fired?
If that's what they want to do, then so be it. I've long passed the stage of working just for money.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: Haha, that's unlikely. At most, they might lower my rank and reduce my bonus a bit. But don't worry, I work for far more than just a paycheck.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: Thank you so much for all you've done, [Trailblazer]. I never thought we'd drag the Express into a crisis again, much less one that might cause a rift between you and the IPC.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: A rift? I wouldn't go that far. Also, it's me who's mostly to blame — I didn't keep my subordinates in check.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: Mind putting in some good words for me with your bosses?
Is it true the IPC requires you to go through 17 rounds of interviews?
Oh? Thinking about a career change?
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: Sure thing! I'll put in the best words I can, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: 17? Oh... I think I might know who you're talking about.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: You could say he's a special case. For most people the interview process is much shorter.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: Hehe, I'm glad we're able to discuss some lighter topics.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: [Trailblazer], you all need some rest after everything you've been through. I've arranged rooms for you all at the Goethe Hotel.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Miss Topaz, if you need somewhere comfortable to stay...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I appreciate the offer, but I need to head back and deliver my reports.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: [Trailblazer], Miss Bronya, it's been great getting to know you both. I hope we can work together again in the future... only next time under better circumstances!
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: (March was looking forward to the Solwarm Festival for ages... Looks like she's missed her chance, this time...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (I never thought this trip would be so... *yawn* ...tiring. Time for bed...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I've always longed for the stars since I was a child, which is why I devoted myself to science and the studying of the Stellaron. If someone told me that I could do whatever research I wanted with only a small price to pay... I probably wouldn't hesitate.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: I can't speak for everyone, but this is how I really feel.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: If the IPC is able to bring about immediate change, then I think that's a price well worth paying.
rows.speaker: Pela

rows.text: Building a better world for future generations sound great, right? But is it any fun for the engineers and Architects who are directly involved in such a pursuit?
rows.speaker: Pela

rows.text: I'm not sure how much weight my opinion carries, but that's my take on the matter.
rows.speaker: Pela

rows.text: Faced with this sort of coercion, we must resist them with all our might! Surrendering is not an option!
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: You must warn the Madam Guardian not to allow herself to fall into their trap!
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: "Those who are willing to give up freedom for security will end up with neither."
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: I hope Bronya takes these words seriously.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: I think if we have a choice for the future, it should be everyone's decision.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Hook, Julian, and The Moles all have different dreams. I don't think anyone should take them away...
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: The truth is, great ambitions and lofty plans no longer hold much appeal to an old-timer like me.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: If this "IPC" does indeed possess the magical power to restore Belobog back to its former self overnight, then I think the answer is clear.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: But that's just my personal opinion. In the end, it's all up to Lady Bronya.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: [Trailblazer], why don't you head over to the Goethe Hotel and relax for a bit? Miss Topaz and I still have a few matters to discuss.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I'm sorry you didn't get to experience the festival atmosphere this time around... I promise I'll make it up to you all next time.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: March, [Trailblazer], you're back.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: So... what's the verdict? What do the people think?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: We talked to people in both the Overworld and Underworld. The final result was... a tie.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I see... I suppose everyone has their own way of seeing things. I can't say I'm surprised.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...What was Seele's perspective on the matter?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: She's behind you, whatever you decide.
She thought it wasn't her place to say.
...I should've known. That sounds like Seele alright.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Did you come to a conclusion with the ministers? It's so loud I can't tell what anyone's saying...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It's pretty much the same situation here. Neither party is willing to compromise.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: The time has to come to make a decision... This chaos cannot be allowed to continue any longer.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Phew, I was worried things were gonna get ugly again. A peaceful solution is always the best solution.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Speaking of solutions... Are they repairing that giant robot — the one we fought against? I remember you took control of it and helped us defeat Cocolia!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I wonder if we'll have time to celebrate the Solwarm Festival.
I hope Topaz's negotiations go smoothly.
Right! I'd totally forgotten — that's the whole reason we came here in the first place!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Looks like everyone in the city's helping with construction — doubt there'll be much time for celebrating. Still, look on the bright side — we got to meet a top IPC executive! The trip wasn't a complete waste, right?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Miss Topaz is definitely up to the job! She has that aura of... what's the word... invincibility!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Well, we didn't get to enjoy the festivities this time round, but at least we still got to meet a top IPC executive!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Y'know, [Trailblazer], I'd heard you and March speak highly of the Supreme Guardian before, but seeing her methods firsthand left me in awe.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: We should also be glad that Miss Topaz is the one in charge of the Jarilo-VI project. If it were someone else from the Strategic Investment Department, things might have gotten... complicated.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: What do you mean, Himeko?
You mean Topaz didn't make things complicated enough?
The Strategic Investment Department comprises the IPC's most elite employees, many of whom can be very... forceful.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: That tells me you really don't understand the Strategic Investment Department, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Let's talk about this later when you're back on the Express. You and March must be tired after such an incredible journey — it's time you got some well-deserved rest.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You only got demoted one rank? Whew, you dodged a bullet there — pretty big project to mess up on. Someone must be looking out for you. Oh, they've already left the call...
Ugh, this voice changer is driving me crazy. Let me turn it off.
...Aventurine? Why are you still on the line?
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: Hey, what's with the hostility? It's not like I'm your boss... Oh, wait, I guess I am now? Haha! My apologies — I'm still getting used to my new place in the hierarchy!
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: ...Can I help you? If you've got something to say, say it already.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: Oh, nothing important — just checking in on you. I told you Jarilo-VI would be a high-risk low-reward case. Why'd you even bother?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: In our line of work, having a kind heart can be more of a liability than an asset. If you're not careful, you'll end up leading yourself down a dead-end road...
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: ...Anything else? If not, I'm hanging up.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: W—Wait, hold on a minute, don't hang up. I get it, you're not in the mood for this conversation right now... Okay, how about this — something that might interest you...
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: While you were enjoying your playtime on Jarilo-VI, Diamond was busy taking care of the head honcho of the Building Material Logistics Department. That's why he didn't attend today's meeting.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Taravan?
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: That's right, the renowned Taravan — one of the seven board members! He's throwing his support behind us instead of the Marketing Development Department for once. Ha! Oswaldo won't be laughing anymore!
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Diamond's been a great help to both of us. Your antics on such a crucial day can't exactly have painted the Strategic Investment Department in a good light, y'know?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Since you get the point, let's get down to business... I'm currently at Pier Point — there's a major deal that could affect the whole department. I just so happen to need a reliable project manager for the job... what do you say, old friend?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Huh, and what prompted the mighty Aventurine to start collaborating with others?
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: Penacony, what else?
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: ...What?
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: That's right⁓ Now that's the kind of reaction I was hoping for.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: Hold on a minute... Diamond picked you for this project? I was expecting someone like Opal or Obsidian to handle it — at least somebody higher than rank P46...
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: Honestly, who knows? "The Family" has some pretty questionable characters. If you ask me, doing business with them is a lost cause.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: But as we both know, the IPC does more than just "business deals" — guess it's my time to shine. So, how about it? This is a rare opportunity. Consider it. You never know, you might even be able to make up for your blunder on Jarilo-VI.
rows.speaker: Aventurine

rows.text: ...I'll get back to you later.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: We've got your back! We failed to convince Topaz, but this should be a piece of cake!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Thank you, March. I'll assemble the ministers. Let's meet up again here later.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: The supreme guardian has briefed me on the situation and asked that I assist you in locating Topaz.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Ready to enter Rivet Town? We'll go in together when everyone is set.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Ready.
Keep your guards up — we might run into IPC agents ahead.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Just a minute.
Take your time — preparation is key.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Perhaps, but the IPC won't wait for me to catch up.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: They're moving quickly. Belobog is crawling with their agents — all they talk about is "asset evaluation."
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: In your eyes, the IPC may seem heartless or cruel, but in reality, we all have a story to tell. As for myself, I was born on a small, unremarkable planet at the edge of the galaxy — a place whose name is known only to the native inhabitants.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: Two years after signing the contract, the dark clouds and haze disappeared, and people began to take off their masks. After three years, vegetation and trees began to grow and thrive again. After five years, many animals — previously on the brink of extinction — reappeared.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: I am writing to you, Miss Bronya, with the genuine desire to express something important...
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: I know freedom is precious to people, but in reality there are things of much greater value... such as survival.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: I hesitate to call it a solution, but I might have some information that might help.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The life of a navigator is a busy one, [Trailblazer]. You should be glad that I made it in time.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Information? Please, tell me what you know, Miss Himeko.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Of course! The Nameless have quite the reputation — you're following in the footsteps of the great Akivili, after all!
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: I'd be surprised if you didn't! Don't underestimate the reputation of the Nameless out among the stars — you're following in the footsteps of the great Akivili, after all!
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: I'm pleased to see how well everyone's been getting along. Topaz, based on your greeting I presume you have a good grasp of the current situation?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You're very curious about my work, aren't you?
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: Haha, I wish!
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: So many eager faces — I won't keep you in the dark any longer.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: I thought you might.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Hey! Shh! That's a secret!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Miss Topaz, I know you've done a lot of research into Belobog. I was wondering if there was any information on the Engine of Creation in your records?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I'm inclined to agree... It's hard to imagine she wrote that letter just to deceive me.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Yes... she is a high-ranking member of the IPC, after all. She knows how to use words to her advantage.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I agree, but it struck me as an honest letter — I found the contents quite moving. It's hard to imagine she'd write something like this just to deceive me.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: In any case, she wasn't wrong when she said this would be an extremely difficult decision.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: That thought has crossed my mind, and it comforts me to hear you say that, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I trust her judgment too, but...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Topaz hasn't given me much time to consider. She wants me to decide as soon as possible.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Yes, we need to move fast.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I... think we should leave this matter to the Belobogians... Don't you agree?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Welcome back. I appreciate your help more than I can express — it couldn't have been easy running all over the city.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: That's what friends are for, Bronya! ...You don't sound like yourself. Is something wrong?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I'm fine, I just... I haven't rested in a while. There's just too much happening all at once...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: The silver lining is that apart from the mine incident you mentioned, there haven't been any major conflicts in other areas. I suppose Topaz must have issued an order against harassing the citizenry.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Still, that hasn't stopped panic from building... People are confused — they don't know where these strangers in black came from, nor what their intentions are.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Did you manage to get in touch with Topaz again? We're curious to know what solution she has in mind...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That's the reason I asked for you to come here. I need your advice.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Look...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: It's...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...The contract Topaz sent to me a little while ago. There's a handwritten letter attached.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Please, take a look at the contents... and then tell me your thoughts.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: This planet's fate, the civilization it carries, everything that has happened here and everything that will happen... it all rests in my hands...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: This definitely can't — and shouldn't — be a decision made by me alone.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Right? I don't think it's fair for you to carry the weight alone. Why not discuss it with others first?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: What if this decision is too much for one person? The impact of this choice could haunt Bronya for the rest of her life.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I wanted to put it to a vote, and let all the citizens of both the Overworld and the Underworld have their say. But with such little time, I'm afraid that's a lost cause.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I'll convene the Qlipoth Fort Architects immediately to discuss the contract. As for the locals, I'd like you to gauge their stance on the matter.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: The people of Belobog hold both of you in high regard. They'll most certainly be willing to tell you their thoughts.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Her words do sound quite sincere... What do you make of it, [Trailblazer]?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: In light of the events that have transpired, we will be taking the following disciplinary measures against you.
Your rank will be demoted from P45 to P44, with corresponding adjustment to your basic salary. All bonuses for the current cycle will be revoked, including stock options and performance bonuses.
You will also need to submit an additional report regarding this incident to Diamond. If you have any objections to this penalty, you may also file an appeal in writing.
I have no objections.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: Understood. Is there anything else anyone would like to add?
If there are no further remarks, this meeting is concluded.
...Do you two recognize that broken-down machine over there?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: It's called the Engine of Creation. Do you remember it?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Not at all... which is why I find it so incredible... Such a massive feat of engineering, yet there's not a single mention of it in any of the Strategic Investment Department's reports.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: I may know the reason why. The Engine of Creation was constructed solely by the people of Belobog, without any external assistance.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: The project was led by the first Supreme Guardian — Alisa Rand. While warriors fought on the front lines, the engineers worked tirelessly behind the scenes, designing and constructing it...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: So what you're saying is... the "Engine of Creation" was a weapon constructed by the Belobogians themselves?
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: Yes, but not entirely.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: The Engine of Creation was commissioned for combat shortly after its completion and played a significant role in the battles against the Legion.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: But Alisa Rand had a long-term vision, one that nobody anticipated. For a long time, this feat of engineering was codenamed the "Geological Reconstruction Unit."
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: It was actually given a much grander purpose: To help the Belobogians rebuild their homeland and restore their world to its former glory... after driving away all those who threatened it.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Remarkable. A vision that would transcend both time and generations of Belobogians. Madam Rand was truly an inspiring leader.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: Not to take away from the Supreme Guardian in front of me... Hehe, she's quite the inspiring leader as well.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: Thank you, but I didn't really do anything.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: All I did was bring the people of Belobog together and make them aware that our hard-earned freedom was under immense threat once again.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: If we want to preserve this freedom, we must act and show those who doubt us that we, Belobog, have the will and the ability to control our own destiny.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: The outcome of our mobilization speaks for itself. The children of Belobog have made their decision. They have chosen to preserve this homeland with their own two hands.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...I must say, I didn't anticipate this at all.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: I'll fight for this opportunity for you, Bronya. I shouldn't have conflated your own circumstances with my childhood. That was a serious lapse of judgment on my part.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: My world never had a resolute leader, so people gave up on the idea of saving themselves long ago. But your civilization has persisted through the snow and storms for 700 years... A truly admirable feat.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: Then, are you willing to retract your previous decision? As for the debt... we'll find a way to gradually repay it, but it'll take some time...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...Unfortunately the acquisition of Jarilo-VI is a strategic decision that's been approved by the IPC's top brass. Even if I wanted to overturn it, convincing them would be extremely difficult.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: Unless...
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: Don't worry, Miss Topaz. Myself and all of the Nameless aboard the Astral Express are willing to vouch for this world.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Fantastic! That might just work. As for the reports and potential accountability...
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: ...I'll handle it.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: Miss Bronya — if you'll permit me to call you that — I'd like to share a story with you from my own life.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: My home planet was extremely resource-poor. To survive, people worked laboriously, manufacturing products for other civilizations in the galaxy — mostly in the chemical or heavy industries.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: Given these circumstances, the natural environment of my home planet became increasingly harsh. I don't recall the exact moment when it happened, but people started wearing respirators just to walk down the street. All you could hear were the wheezing coughs of the people — day and night.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: My home was facing its demise. The relatively wealthy chose interstellar migration and started anew. The majority who stayed could only struggle on amidst sewage, acid rain, and dust, waiting for the end.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: Finally, one fateful day, the IPC arrived on my home planet. They had the technology to repair our planet's damaged environment. In return for their help, they asked for just one thing — that all inhabitants sign a contract which would make them employees of the IPC.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: When I was finally old enough, I officially became a member of the Strategic Investment Department. I witnessed the changes that took place on my home world and was determined to bring the same changes to many other worlds in the galaxy that were experiencing the same plight.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: How many generations of Belobogians will it take to embrace the stars again without assistance? Who can guarantee that every future Guardian will be as prudent and enlightened as you? How can you guarantee that a disaster such as the Stellaron Crisis will not descend upon Belobog yet again?
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: I have already negotiated the best possible deal for you. Once you sign this contract, all of Belobog's debts will be forgiven. In addition, the IPC will set up a special team to support the reconstruction of Jarilo-VI.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: I can understand that for you, this is an extremely difficult decision, because you, and you alone will bear the fate of all Belobogians.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: But because of this, I believe that you will make the right decision — a decision that will truly benefit your people.
rows.speaker: Topaz

rows.text: Hey, [Trailblazer], did you hear about our next stop? It's a world called "Penacony" — I hear it's a beautiful, dreamy place... I'm so excited...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...but Pom-Pom said the banquet we were invited to is still a little ways off. Hmm... what can I do to pass the time...?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...Huh? Is that my phone? Must be the group chat.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That Dan Heng — he can't just ignore Bronya...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Let's go to his room and talk to him.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: He won't budge, huh? Looks like it's just the two of us then.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Pity, he's gonna miss out! We never get the chance to go on a stress-free adventure.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: He's been through a lot lately.
I know... But it's still a shame, don't you think?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Stress-free for us, or stress-free for the planet?
Don't get yourself all worked up. If Jarilo-VI is strong enough to withstand a Stellaron, it'll be just fine.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: If only Himeko could come with us...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Should we ask Mr. Yang to come with us?
Mm, maybe not. He's still wheezing from the trouble we got into on the Xianzhou. You didn't notice?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: At his age, he might not appreciate the extra... excitement.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: What about Pom-Pom?
Pom-Pom can't just leave the Express whenever they feel like it. You didn't know?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Seems like someone wasn't paying attention!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: [Trailblazer], why don't we go ask Himeko to tag along? She might be up for an adventure!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You've been on the Express for a while now, but you've never gone on a trip with Himeko before, right? Well, now's your chance!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: When did you buy it?
Very fancy!
Brr! How do people living in all this snow celebrate anything...?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: One thing's for sure though, [Trailblazer]. Where there's a celebration, there's bound to be food, right?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Come on Belobog... don't let me down.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That's us. The honor is yours.
We may have helped out a little bit.
Teach me how to get rich!
I'm in charge of a project worth 8 billion credits, by the way.
Hang on a sec, isn't that Wallace up ahead? Looks like he's finally made some friends! I wonder what they're talking about...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Is that Pela? Looks like she's teaching the kids again.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: [Trailblazer], quick! Serval's about to start singing!
rows.speaker: March 7th
